about.title: Chula Vista Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Chula Vista sits between the bay and the Otay foothills, and most of its 265,757 residents get around by car. That reliance shows up in the public record: in 2025, the city logged 940 injury collisions, 1,308 people hurt, and 15 traffic deaths. Corridors like Broadway, Olympic Parkway, Main Street, and 4th Avenue carry a large share of those reports, and the counts tend to climb on Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. as commuters head home. If one of those crashes involved you, the days that follow can feel scattered, with medical visits, a car in the shop, and an adjuster who wants a statement before you have even sorted out what happened. We are here to steady that process. Our team handles San Diego County car accident claims. Tell us about your collision and we will review your case at no cost. You pay nothing upfront, and we collect a fee only if there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Chula Vista Drivers Choose Us

items.title: California's Deadlines Are Real
items.desc: Most car accident claims in California must be filed within two years, but if a city, county, or state vehicle was involved, a government claim may be due in as little as six months. Getting started early gives us room to work.

items.title: Fault Is Shared, Not All-or-Nothing
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if an insurer says you were partly to blame, you can still pursue a claim reduced by your share. We can push back when that share is inflated.

items.title: Your Words and Evidence Matter
items.desc: The other driver's insurer may ask for a recorded statement quickly; you are not required to give one before speaking with an attorney. Photos, dashcam footage, witness contacts, and medical records should be saved right away.

items.question: I was hit on Olympic Parkway and the other driver's insurer keeps calling. What should I do?
items.answer: You can politely decline to give a recorded statement until you have spoken with an attorney. Write down what you remember, keep every photo and repair estimate, and save any dashcam or nearby business footage before it is overwritten. Then contact us and we will handle those calls for you.

items.question: Does it cost anything to hire an attorney?
items.answer: Our initial case review is free. We work on contingency, meaning we are paid a percentage only if your claim results in a recovery. If nothing is recovered, you owe no attorney fee.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover for pain and suffering in a California car accident case?
items.answer: California places no cap on non-economic damages, such as pain, suffering, and loss of enjoyment of life, in ordinary car accident cases. Your actual recovery depends on the facts, the available insurance, and how fault is allocated under comparative negligence. We can review the specifics of your Chula Vista crash and explain what may apply to you.
